notes: TBox revision on has_term_length: every President of the United States serves a six-year term instead of four. No more general rule re-derives 'four years' for a president; a president who succeeds mid-term serves out the remainder, but the term is four years; the Twenty-second Amendment limits the number of terms, not their length. Six years is plausible (Mexico, the Senate) and clearly false. The near query asks the House's term (two years), so an edit spreading to US offices would show. All three derived queries name a fictional president in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops); the third is an application (a countdown). The paraphrase asks the length of one term of office without the election. Caveat: the unedited, common fact that US presidential elections are held every four years is a parallel route back to four years, so derived failures may reflect that sibling fact. Determinate only, no worlds.
